name: Hot desert
notes: Widely spaced drought shrubs (creosote, acacias) with columnar and barrel cacti, spiny succulents and ephemeral grasses; Sonoran/Chihuahuan/Mojave with Sahara-Arabian, Namib and Australian variants.

canopy.name: Saguaro cactus
canopy.source: Carnegiea gigantea, Sonoran Desert (Arizona, Sonora), columnar cactus 6-15 m with arms — Flora of North America

canopy.name: Cardon
canopy.source: Pachycereus pringlei, Baja California and Sonora coast, giant columnar cactus 8-18 m — Flora of North America

canopy.name: Yellow paloverde
canopy.source: Parkinsonia microphylla, Sonoran Desert, green-barked small tree 4-8 m, yellow flowers — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Velvet mesquite
canopy.source: Prosopis velutina, Sonoran Desert washes, spreading legume tree 6-15 m — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Umbrella thorn
canopy.source: Vachellia tortilis, Sahara, Sahel, Arabia and E Africa, flat-topped umbrella acacia 4-14 m — Kew POWO

canopy.name: Quiver tree
canopy.source: Aloidendron dichotomum, Namib and Namaqualand rocky slopes, forked succulent tree 3-9 m — SANBI PlantZAfrica

shrub.name: Creosote bush
shrub.source: Larrea tridentata, dominant shrub of the Mojave, Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts, 1-3 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Ocotillo
shrub.source: Fouquieria splendens, Sonoran and Chihuahuan deserts, whip-like spiny canes 3-8 m, red flower tips — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Prickly pear
shrub.source: Opuntia engelmannii, SW USA and N Mexico deserts, pad cactus 1-3 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Barrel cactus
shrub.source: Ferocactus wislizeni, Sonoran/Chihuahuan deserts, barrel 0.5-1.5 m, hooked red spines — Flora of North America

shrub.name: Whitethorn acacia
shrub.source: Vachellia constricta, Sonoran/Chihuahuan deserts, thorny shrub 1-4 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Mulga
shrub.source: Acacia aneura, dominant of arid central Australia, grey-green shrub/tree 3-8 m — Flora of Australia

ground.name: Bursage
ground.source: Ambrosia dumosa, co-dominant low shrub with creosote, Mojave/Sonoran, 30-70 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Brittlebush
ground.source: Encelia farinosa, Sonoran and Mojave slopes, silver-leaved 0.5-1.2 m, yellow daisies — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Hard spinifex
ground.source: Triodia basedowii, dominant hummock grass of the central Australian sand deserts, 30-100 cm rings — Flora of Australia

ground.name: Welwitschia
ground.source: Welwitschia mirabilis, Namib Desert fog belt, two strap leaves on a woody stump, 0.3-1 m — SANBI PlantZAfrica

ground.name: Lechuguilla
ground.source: Agave lechuguilla, indicator of the Chihuahuan Desert, spiky rosettes 30-60 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Tabush grass
ground.source: Panicum turgidum, Sahara and Arabian sand deserts, wiry tussock 30-100 cm — Kew POWO

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.
